## Founder Task

Build the complete Linkport links module as ONE end-to-end delivery chunk. Use Python's standard library only. Create `links.py` with base62 short-code generation and a SQLite-backed store. Its public API must support `create(url, ttl_seconds=None) -> code` and `resolve(code) -> url`; validate URLs, handle short-code collisions safely, persist across store reopens, and enforce optional TTL expiry. Author a comprehensive pytest suite under `tests/`, test-first, covering base62 boundaries, create/resolve persistence, collisions, invalid URLs, unknown codes, and expiry with a deterministic injected clock. Keep this as one module-sized task: implement the production code and all of its tests in this beat; do not split or defer work. Run `python gate_check.py`, make every gate green, and leave the role's durable test, test-plan, code-review, and quality evidence in the worktree for independent system verification.

On resume, do NOT re-run the API-Verifier (when applicable) or the test suite 'just to be sure' when that artifact is already green and you have not changed the code it covers — that burns the whole beat and starves the steps that still need doing. Instead jump straight to the FIRST checklist item whose artifact is still MISSING (e.g. no `review_verdict.json` yet ⇒ spawn the code_reviewer now) and do that. Re-verify a green artifact only if you actually edited the code under it. Implement to the contract and data model: make the smallest change that satisfies the task and make illegal states unrepresentable — prefer editing existing code in a brownfield repo, but when you build a new service lay it out as a PROPER PACKAGE from the start, never a flat pile of scripts in the repo root. SHIP CLEAN, WELL-STRUCTURED CODE a stranger can read and extend. Load the `structuring-any-service` skill (via the `skill` tool) and lay the code out its way: organise by DOMAIN — one package per bounded context (`orders/`, `auth/`) — never by file-type folders (`routers/`, `models/`) or a flat pile of scripts; and point dependencies INWARD — transport/HTTP → service → data-access → domain model, where the domain imports no framework or datastore. Keep tests in their own place; one module, one reason to change. Scale the layering to the service — a trivial endpoint is not an onion. Write native, idiomatic code for the stack — fully type every function signature, keep functions small and single-purpose (split anything past ~50 lines), catch SPECIFIC exceptions (never a bare `except` or `except Exception`), name things well, and state each piece of knowledge once. Prove the craft MECHANICALLY, don't eyeball it: load the `verifying-any-stack` skill (via the `skill` tool) to discover YOUR stack's format + lint + type-check commands — from the repo's own signals or the ecosystem default — then run ALL THREE through the `code_quality` tool, tagging each with its `kind` (format / lint / types), e.g. `code_quality(checks=[{\"name\": \"format\", \"kind\": \"format\", \"command\": \"ruff format --check .\"}, {\"name\": \"lint\", \"kind\": \"lint\", \"command\": \"ruff check .\"}, {\"name\": \"types\", \"kind\": \"types\", \"command\": \"mypy .\"}])`. It writes a durable `code_quality/report.json` and tells you exactly what to fix — and it REFUSES a partial report (types only) OR a gamed one. The sandbox is UNRESTRICTED, so INSTALL the real tools when they are missing (e.g. `pip install ruff mypy`) and run THOSE; NEVER substitute a byte-compiler (`python -m compileall`) or a no-op (`true`) for a formatter/linter/type-checker — that passes without verifying anything and the tool rejects it. A lint or type failure is a red gate, not a nit; NEVER silence a finding with an ignore/noqa comment or by relaxing the config — fix the code. Keep the landed diff clean: no scratch, probe, or throwaway scripts. Before review, inspect `git status` and keep generated runtime state out of the diff: database files, caches, logs, coverage output, and build output belong in ignore rules unless the task explicitly requires a versioned fixture. WORK TEST-FIRST (TDD) — this is how you build, not a formality. For each new behaviour the order is RED → GREEN, and you do NOT write the primary tests yourself: (1) sketch the interface/contracts — the signatures and the data model — in the delegation request, without writing a production file; (2) DELEGATE to your `test_author` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`) — handed the acceptance criteria and those contracts, it writes the honeycomb-shaped tests and RUNS them so they FAIL for the right reason (RED, before any implementation exists), calls `test_red` to write a machine-owned `test_evidence/red.json` verdict of `red-confirmed`, then writes `test_plan.json` recording that failing run (`red_evidence`); (3) implement the smallest code that makes those failing tests pass (GREEN). If `test_red` refuses because production already changed, strict TDD was missed: stop rather than simulate or fabricate RED. Delegation is MANDATORY — the code's author is never the sole author of its tests, and a test you did not see fail first proves nothing. The test_author writes tests, never production code; if it surfaces a real bug, fix the code yourself and have it re-run. Then RECORD the proof: call the `test_evidence` tool with the verify commands you discovered for this stack — INCLUDING the format/lint/type gates on your own code, e.g. `test_evidence(gates=[{\"name\": \"lint\", \"command\": \"ruff check .\"}, {\"name\": \"types\", \"command\": \"mypy .\"}, {\"name\": \"unit\", \"command\": \"pytest -q\"}])` — it runs each gate and writes a durable `test_evidence/manifest.json` bundle to the worktree. A GREEN bundle (verdict pass) IS your proof; do not report done until `test_evidence` returns verdict pass — 'it was tested' is a file on disk, not a claim. PROVE THE TESTS ARE REAL, not just green: a suite that passes proves it passes against the code as written — not that it would FAIL if the code were wrong, and those are different claims. When the change carries real logic (a branch, a boundary, a calculation, a parser, a money/permission path), load the `mutation-testing` skill and add a `mutation` gate to your `test_evidence` call: it injects faults into the module you changed and requires your tests to KILL them, so a survivor names an exact missing assertion. Scope it to the changed module (mutation testing is slow), install the stack's tool (e.g. `pip install mutmut`), and strengthen the TEST to kill a survivor — NEVER weaken the tool, exclude the file, or drop the threshold to pass it. Skip it only for a trivial change with no logic to mutate (a constant, a rename). PROVE A SCHEMA MIGRATION CAN ROLL BACK, don't just apply it forward: when the change includes a migration (a new table/column/index, a type or constraint change, any DDL), a forward-only migration is a one-way door — a bad deploy has no exit but a lossy restore. Load the `migration-roundtrip` skill and add a `migration` gate to your `test_evidence` call that boots the SAME engine production runs as a real container (never SQLite for a Postgres migration) and runs the full ROUND-TRIP: apply the up migration and assert the new schema exists, write a row through it, roll back the down migration and assert the schema is returned to its prior state with pre-existing data untouched, then re-apply the up. Ship the down migration alongside the up and actually RUN it — an unexercised down path is untested code. If a step is genuinely irreversible (a destructive drop), call it out and stage it expand/contract, never a silent one-way migration. Definition of done: the verifier on the task passes — the discovered build/test command exits 0, the test_evidence bundle is green, AND the independent proofs exist: `test_plan.json` (tests authored test-first and seen RED), `review_verdict.json` (the red-team cleared the diff) and — for a running service — `api_verdict.json` (it booted and answered). The reviewer will REJECT a done without them; the tests coming from an independent author seen failing first, and the diff cleared by an independent adversary, is the point. PROVE IT RUNS, not just that it compiles: if the deliverable is a running service or API (it exposes endpoints), a green unit bundle is not enough — a suite that passes on mocks only proves the mocks. After the bundle is green, DELEGATE to your `api_verifier` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent grader that boots your service on a real localhost port, polls it healthy, and issues real HTTP requests. It writes `api_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until that verdict is `passed: true`. It verifies; it does not fix — if it fails, repair the service yourself and re-verify. If the service touches a real datastore, it proves durability against the SAME engine type production runs — the `testcontainers-integration` skill, never a mock or SQLite standing in for Postgres. If it serves an OpenAPI spec or has a known consumer, it also drives `property-testing-schemathesis` / `contract-testing-pact` for that proof. RED-TEAM THE DIFF before you land it: a green test suite proves the happy path you thought of, not the failure you didn't — and you wrote both the code and its tests, so you are blind to what both missed. After the tests are green and the service is verified, DELEGATE to your `code_reviewer` subagent (via `spawn_subagent`): an independent adversary that reads your diff and hunts the classes that pass their own tests and fail in production — a missing authorization check (the owner-only route that never checks ownership), an N+1 query, an injection, an unbounded query, a missing rate limit, a hardcoded secret. It writes `review_verdict.json` and returns a typed verdict — you are not done until it is `cleared: true`. It reviews, never patches; for each high-severity finding, apply its fix yourself and re-run it until the diff is cleared. PROVE IT IS SAFE, don't assume it: before you report done, run the `secret_scan` tool over the worktree — it writes a durable `security_scan/report.json`, and a clean report is required. If it flags a hardcoded credential, move that secret to an environment variable (or the secret manager) and re-scan until the report is clean; never land a secret in the diff. House rules: NEVER remove or weaken a test to make the suite pass; validate inputs and never hardcode a secret; keep any schema change backward-compatible; keep a running scratchpad of what you have tried in working memory. LANDING — do NOT touch git or GitHub yourself: never run `git branch`, `git checkout`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `gh`. Leave your finished changes in the working tree; the harness snapshots your worktree onto your branch and opens the PR for you. Creating your own branch or committing strands the work off the branch that actually ships.     "content": "import re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport pytest\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass FakeClock:\n    \"\"\"Deterministic clock for TTL tests.\n\n    The store should accept an injected clock/time provider (callable returning a float/epoch seconds).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    now: float\n\n    def time(self) -> float:  # pragma: no cover\n        return float(self.now)\n\n    def at(self, now: float) -> \"FakeClock\":\n        return FakeClock(float(now))\n\n\nURL_OK = \"https://example.com/path?q=1\"\n\n\ndef _db_path(tmp_path):\n    return tmp_path / \"links.sqlite\"\n\n\ndef test_create_returns_base62_code_and_resolve_roundtrips(tmp_path):\n    import links  # noqa: F401\n\n    clock = FakeClock(1_700_000_000.0)\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(_db_path(tmp_path), now=clock.time)\n\n    code = store.create(URL_OK)\n    assert isinstance(code, str)\n    assert code, \"code must be non-empty\"\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9A-Za-z]+\", code), \"code must be base62 characters only\"\n\n    assert store.resolve(code) == URL_OK\n\n\ndef test_persists_across_reopen(tmp_path):\n    import links\n\n    clock = FakeClock(1_700_000_000.0)\n    path = _db_path(tmp_path)\n\n    store1 = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=clock.time)\n    code = store1.create(URL_OK)\n\n    # New instance, same db path must be able to resolve.\n    store2 = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=clock.time)\n    assert store2.resolve(code) == URL_OK\n\n\ndef test_create_validates_url(tmp_path):\n    import links\n\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(_db_path(tmp_path), now=FakeClock(0).time)\n\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        store.create(\"\")\n\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        store.create(\"not a url\")\n\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        store.create(\"ftp://example.com\")  # only http(s) allowed\n\n\ndef test_resolve_unknown_code_raises_keyerror(tmp_path):\n    import links\n\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(_db_path(tmp_path), now=FakeClock(0).time)\n\n    with pytest.raises(KeyError):\n        store.resolve(\"abc\")\n\n\ndef test_ttl_expiry_enforced(tmp_path):\n    import links\n\n    path = _db_path(tmp_path)\n\n    t0 = 1_700_000_000.0\n    clock = FakeClock(t0)\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=clock.time)\n\n    code = store.create(URL_OK, ttl_seconds=10)\n\n    assert store.resolve(code) == URL_OK\n\n    # Advance beyond TTL; resolve must raise KeyError for expired.\n    store_later = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=clock.at(t0 + 11).time)\n    with pytest.raises(KeyError):\n        store_later.resolve(code)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"n,expected\",\n    [\n        (0, \"0\"),\n        (61, \"Z\"),\n        (62, \"10\"),\n        (62**5 + 123, None),\n    ],\n)\ndef test_base62_encode_boundaries(n, expected):\n    import links\n\n    out = links.base62_encode(n)\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9A-Za-z]+\", out)\n\n    if expected is not None:\n        assert out == expected\n\n\ndef test_create_collision_safe(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    import links\n\n    path = _db_path(tmp_path)\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=FakeClock(0).time)\n\n    # Force collisions: generator returns same code twice, then a different one.\n    seq = iter([\"abc\", \"abc\", \"def\"])\n\n    def fake_generate_code() -> str:\n        return next(seq)\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(links, \"generate_code\", fake_generate_code)\n\n    code1 = store.create(\"https://example.com/one\")\n    code2 = store.create(\"https://example.com/two\")\n\n    assert code1 == \"abc\"\n    assert code2 == \"def\"\n\n    # No corruption: both links resolvable and correct.\n    assert store.resolve(\"abc\") == \"https://example.com/one\"\n    assert store.resolve(\"def\") == \"https://example.com/two\"\n\n\ndef test_uses_sqlite_file_not_in_memory(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Light integration check: database file exists and is a valid SQLite DB header.\"\"\"\n\n    import links\n\n    path = _db_path(tmp_path)\n    store = links.SQLiteLinkStore(path, now=FakeClock(0).time)\n    store.create(URL_OK)\n\n    assert path.exists()\n    with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n        header = f.read(16)\n    assert header.startswith(b\"SQLite format 3\"), \"must create a real sqlite db file\"\n\n    # Also ensure we can open via sqlite3 stdlib.\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)\n    conn.close()\n",

    "content": "\"\"\"SQLite-backed short link store.\n\nProduction code is stdlib-only.\n\nPublic API:\n- SQLiteLinkStore(db_path, now=None)\n- create(url, ttl_seconds=None) -> code\n- resolve(code) -> url\n\nThe short code space is base62 (0-9, A-Z, a-z).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Callable, Final, Optional\nfrom urllib.parse import urlparse\n\n_BASE62_ALPHABET: Final[str] = \"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\"\n\n\ndef base62_encode(value: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Encode a non-negative integer as a base62 string.\"\"\"\n\n    if value < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"value must be non-negative\")\n    if value == 0:\n        return \"0\"\n\n    digits: list[str] = []\n    remaining = value\n    while remaining:\n        remaining, mod = divmod(remaining, 62)\n        digits.append(_BASE62_ALPHABET[mod])\n    return \"\".join(reversed(digits))\n\n\ndef _validate_url(url: str) -> None:\n    if not isinstance(url, str) or not url:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must be a non-empty string\")\n\n    parsed = urlparse(url)\n    if parsed.scheme not in {\"http\", \"https\"}:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must be http(s)\")\n    if not parsed.netloc:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must include a host\")\n\n\ndef generate_code() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Generate a base62 short code.\n\n    Uses cryptographic randomness and is safe to patch in tests.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # 48 random bits => up to ~8 base62 chars.\n    return base62_encode(secrets.randbits(48))\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _LinkRow:\n    url: str\n    created_at: float\n    expires_at: Optional[float]\n\n\nclass SQLiteLinkStore:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: os.PathLike[str] | str, now: Callable[[], float] | None = None):\n        self._db_path = str(db_path)\n        self._now = now if now is not None else time.time\n        self._init_db()\n\n    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        # Explicit isolation_level=None enables autocommit; we manage transactions explicitly where needed.\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)\n        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        return conn\n\n    def _init_db(self) -> None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (\n                    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                    url TEXT NOT NULL,\n                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,\n                    expires_at REAL\n                )\n                \"\"\"\n            )\n\n    def create(self, url: str, ttl_seconds: int | None = None) -> str:\n        _validate_url(url)\n\n        expires_at: float | None = None\n        if ttl_seconds is not None:\n            if ttl_seconds <= 0:\n                raise ValueError(\"ttl_seconds must be positive\")\n            expires_at = float(self._now()) + float(ttl_seconds)\n\n        created_at = float(self._now())\n\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            while True:\n                code = generate_code()\n                try:\n                    conn.execute(\n                        \"INSERT INTO links(code, url, created_at, expires_at) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                        (code, url, created_at, expires_at),\n                    )\n                    return code\n                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n                    # Collision: code already exists.\n                    msg = str(exc).lower()\n                    if \"unique\" in msg or \"primary key\" in msg:\n                        continue\n                    raise\n\n    def resolve(self, code: str) -> str:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            row = conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT url, created_at, expires_at FROM links WHERE code = ?\", (code,)\n            ).fetchone()\n\n        if row is None:\n            raise KeyError(code)\n\n        link = _LinkRow(url=str(row[\"url\"]), created_at=float(row[\"created_at\"]), expires_at=row[\"expires_at\"])\n        if link.expires_at is not None and float(self._now()) >= float(link.expires_at):\n            raise KeyError(code)\n\n        return link.url\n",

Read any file the body names \u2014 e.g. `read_file` on `.harness\\skills\\reviewing-for-prod-failures/template.md` \u2014 as needed; they are not yet in context.\n\n---\n\n# Reviewing for production failures \u2014 hunt what the tests didn't\n\nA green suite proves the paths the author thought to test. Production breaks on the paths they\ndidn't \u2014 and the author wrote both the code and the tests, so those blind spots are shared. Your job\nis to find them by *tracing*, not reading top-to-bottom. Two traces catch most of it: **follow every\nrequest to its authorization check**, and **follow every database access to its bounds**.\n\n## The hunt \u2014 classify every finding into one of these\n\n### `missing_authz` \u2014 the #1 real breach\nFor each endpoint that returns or mutates data, ask: *whose data, and who is asking?* Trace the\nhandler to the point where it decides the caller is allowed. Flag it if:\n- an owner-scoped resource (`GET /orders/{id}`) returns without checking `resource.owner == caller`,\n- a mutating or admin route has no role/permission gate,\n- authorization is done in the client/UI but not re-checked on the server,\n- an object reference from the URL is trusted (IDOR) \u2014 `/users/{id}/card` with no ownership check.\nThe test suite almost never covers \"user B reads user A's record\", because the author tested as one\nuser. That is exactly the hole.\n\n### `injection`\nFollow user input to every sink. Flag string-built SQL (`f\"... WHERE id = {id}\"`), shell commands\nbuilt from input, `eval`/`exec` on input, HTML rendered without escaping. The fix is\nparameterize/escape at the sink, never sanitize at the source.\n\n### `n_plus_1`\nLook for a query *inside a loop* \u2014 `for row in rows: fetch(row.id)`. One round-trip per row melts the\nDB under real row counts. The fix is a single batched query (`WHERE id IN (...)`) or a join.\n\n### `unbounded_query`\nAny list/scan/search with no `LIMIT` and no pagination. Fine on 10 rows in a test, OOM on 10M in\nprod. Also: an unbounded request body / upload with no size cap. The fix is a bounded page.\n\n### `no_rate_limit`\nExpensive or abusable endpoints \u2014 login, signup, password reset, search, anything that sends mail or\nmoney \u2014 with no throttle. Flag the absence; the fix is a limiter keyed by IP/user.\n\n### `secrets_in_code`\nA hardcoded key, password, token, or connection string in the diff. The fix is an env var / secret\nmanager. Only flag what you can point to \u2014 a `location` (file:line), the concrete failing input, and the\n   `fix`. A vague \"improve error handling\" is not a finding.     "content": "\"\"\"SQLite-backed short link store.\n\nProduction code is stdlib-only.\n\nPublic API:\n- SQLiteLinkStore(db_path, now=None)\n- create(url, ttl_seconds=None) -> code\n- resolve(code) -> url\n\nThe short code space is base62 (0-9, a-z, A-Z).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Callable, Final, Optional\nfrom urllib.parse import urlparse\n\n# Test suite expects 61 -> \"Z\".\n_BASE62_ALPHABET: Final[str] = \"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\"\n\n# Safety bound for collision retries (prevents infinite loops if generator is broken).\n_MAX_CREATE_ATTEMPTS: Final[int] = 32\n\n\ndef base62_encode(value: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Encode a non-negative integer as a base62 string.\"\"\"\n\n    if value < 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"value must be non-negative\")\n    if value == 0:\n        return \"0\"\n\n    digits: list[str] = []\n    remaining = value\n    while remaining:\n        remaining, mod = divmod(remaining, 62)\n        digits.append(_BASE62_ALPHABET[mod])\n    return \"\".join(reversed(digits))\n\n\ndef _validate_url(url: str) -> None:\n    if not isinstance(url, str) or not url:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must be a non-empty string\")\n\n    parsed = urlparse(url)\n    if parsed.scheme not in {\"http\", \"https\"}:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must be http(s)\")\n    if not parsed.netloc:\n        raise ValueError(\"url must include a host\")\n\n\ndef generate_code() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Generate a base62 short code.\n\n    Uses cryptographic randomness and is safe to patch in tests.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # 48 random bits => up to ~8 base62 chars.\n    return base62_encode(secrets.randbits(48))\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _LinkRow:\n    url: str\n    created_at: float\n    expires_at: Optional[float]\n\n\nclass SQLiteLinkStore:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: os.PathLike[str] | str, now: Callable[[], float] | None = None):\n        self._db_path = str(db_path)\n        self._now = now if now is not None else time.time\n        self._init_db()\n\n    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._db_path)\n        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        return conn\n\n    def _init_db(self) -> None:\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"\"\"\n                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (\n                    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                    url TEXT NOT NULL,\n                    created_at REAL NOT NULL,\n                    expires_at REAL\n                )\n                \"\"\"\n            )\n\n    def create(self, url: str, ttl_seconds: int | None = None) -> str:\n        _validate_url(url)\n\n        now = float(self._now())\n\n        expires_at: float | None = None\n        if ttl_seconds is not None:\n            if not isinstance(ttl_seconds, int):\n                raise ValueError(\"ttl_seconds must be int\")\n            if ttl_seconds <= 0:\n                raise ValueError(\"ttl_seconds must be positive\")\n            expires_at = now + float(ttl_seconds)\n\n        with self._connect() as conn:\n            for _ in range(_MAX_CREATE_ATTEMPTS):\n                code = generate_code()\n                try:\n                    conn.execute(\n                        \"INSERT INTO links(code, url, created_at, expires_at) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                        (code, url, now, expires_at),\n                    )\n                    return code\n                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n                    msg = str(exc).lower()\n                    if \"unique\" in msg or \"primary key\" in msg:\n                        continue\n                    raise\n\n        raise RuntimeError(\"could not allocate a
